newsitem.title: NORWAY: OECD sees possible wage inflation in Norway.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees possible wage inflation in Norway.

text.p: Norway's mainland economy may now be operating near capacity amid strong demand pressure, heightening the risk of renewed wage inflation, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Thursday.

In an economic outlook, the OECD said the Norwegian economy had continued its vigorous expansion which started in 1993. Overall GDP, including offshore oil activities and mainland industries, grew by 4.75 percent in 1996 because of strong exports and buoyant demand conditions at home.
"The mainland economy may now be operating at the limit of capacity while demand pressure...continues strong. This situation heightens the risk of renewed wage inflation," the report said.
It said overall economic growth in oil-rich Norway was projected to taper off to around 3.5 percent in 1998 with the upturn of mainland business investment petering out.

"Capital formation on the continental shelf, however, is projected to rebound sharply in 1997," the OECD said. "Moreover, both traditional and petroleum exports should remain buoyant in line with developments abroad."

Accordingly, the mainland economy was envisaged to expand by almost three percent this year and 2.5 percent next year, with the unemployment rate declining to four percent by the end of the projection period.
Wage and price inflation were expected to remain moderate at around 4.5 percent and 2.5 percent respectively.
"However, the tightening labour market risks eroding wage discipline, which might contribute to higher inflationary pressure," the OECD outlook said.
